channel.title: The Daily Stack
channel.description: An automatically generated personal daily podcast in two parts. First, new AI product features from the major labs and the tools built on them: what shipped, how people use it, how you'd try it, and what informed commentators think, with a one-week-later follow-up. Then a lesson from an ongoing course on software development and AI: how software gets built, programming languages and their history, how LLMs work, agents and tools, and the real evidence on AI adoption and value. Each lesson ends with the thirty-second version you could use to explain it to someone else.
channel.itunes:subtitle: A daily class in software and AI, plus the new AI features worth knowing about.

item.title: The software development lifecycle, and where the time really goes · plus: GPT-6.1 Terra and Siri memory
item.description:
OpenAI's new GPT-6.1 Terra is a faster, cheaper mid-tier model built for computer use and reading documents and drawings. iOS 27.2 gives Siri AI a memory of past conversations and more of your personal context to draw on. Then the lesson: the six stages of the software lifecycle, the evidence that maintenance and understanding existing code take most of the effort, and why that matters for judging AI coding claims.
In this episode: • Introducing GPT-6.1 Terra — OpenAI • ChatGPT updates (release notes mirror) — Releasebot (OpenAI release notes) • OpenAI upgrades ChatGPT and Codex with new GPT-6.1 Terra model — 9to5Mac • OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra for precise computer use — TestingCatalog • GPT-6.1 Terra — Simon Willison • GPT-6.1 Terra pushes the cost efficiency frontier — Artificial Analysis • GPT-6.1 Terra Review: Pricing, Benchmarks & Hands-On Tests — Oasis • About iOS 27 Updates — Apple Support • Siri AI is available in more languages starting today — Apple Newsroom • iOS 27.2 is here and Siri AI now remembers your conversations — Absolute Geeks • Information Technology: Agencies Need to Develop Modernization Plans for Critical Legacy Systems (GAO-19-471) — U.S. Government Accountability Office • Software Maintenance Management: A Study of the Maintenance of Computer Application Software in 487 Data Processing Organizations (Lientz and Swanson, 1980) — Addison-Wesley / Computer History Museum catalog • Lientz and Swanson on Software Maintenance — DZone • Revisiting The Facts and Fallacies of Software Engineering (Robert Glass) — Coding Horror • Measuring Program Comprehension: A Large-Scale Field Study with Professionals (Xia et al., IEEE TSE 2018) — Monash University / IEEE • Today was a Good Day: The Daily Life of Software Developers (Meyer, Barr, Bird, Zimmermann, IEEE TSE 2019) — Microsoft Research • Developers spend most of their time figuring systems out — Glamorous Toolkit • Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity — METR

item.title: What code actually is: from transistors to Python
item.description:
A quiet news day, so this episode is all lesson: the first of the course. We climb the layers of abstraction from transistors and machine code, through Kathleen Booth's assembly language, Grace Hopper's compiler and IBM's FORTRAN, up to Python, libraries and frameworks. We look at why every layer trades control for productivity, why abstractions leak, and what that means for the claim that English is the newest programming language.
In this episode: • Claude release notes — Anthropic • ChatGPT updates (release notes mirror) — Releasebot (OpenAI release notes) • Gemini Apps release updates and improvements — Google • Artificial intelligence coverage — TechCrunch • Apple unveils M3, M3 Pro, and M3 Max — Apple Newsroom • Kathleen Booth: Assembling Early Computers While Inventing Assembly — Hackaday • RIP: Kathleen Booth, the inventor of assembly language — The Register • Grace Hopper completes the A-0 compiler — Centre for Computing History • Fortran — IBM • John Backus biography — MacTutor, University of St Andrews • A technological review of the FORTRAN I compiler — Frances E. Allen, IBM (1982) • The Law of Leaky Abstractions (via Simon Willison's 2002 link post) — Joel Spolsky / Simon Willison • On the foolishness of "natural language programming" (EWD667) — Edsger W. Dijkstra • Quote Origin: The Hottest New Programming Language Is English — Quote Investigator • New Jersey seeks COBOL programmers to fix unemployment system — CNBC • COBOL Cowboys Aim To Rescue Sluggish State Unemployment Systems — NPR

item.title: Claude Duet, Anthropic's always-on agent; Gemini Notebook inside Gemini chat
item.description:
Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a separate app where Claude watches your connected apps, sends a morning brief, and works on tasks in the background, asking first before it sends, pays or signs anything. Early reviews are split. Also: Google made Gemini Notebook a connected app, so you can work with your notebooks from inside an ordinary Gemini chat.
In this episode: • Introducing Claude Duet — Anthropic • Claude release notes (Duet launch; Duet safety, privacy, and security) — Releasebot (Anthropic release notes) • Anthropic Launches Claude Duet, a Proactive AI Agent — MacRumors • Vibe Check: Duet—Anthropic's Always-on Agent — Every (Dan Shipper) • Claude Duet discussion — Hacker News • Take actions on your notebooks from Gemini Notebook directly in the Gemini app — Google Workspace Updates • Organise your projects with notebooks in Gemini Apps — Google Gemini Help
